queue.tree_name: The Dragon Tree of the Goethe-Institut Garden
queue.recognise: A grey, heavily forking dragon tree with a wide umbrella crown of leaf tufts, standing in the middle of the garden cafe's terrace.
queue.story:
A reader found this one, in the garden of the Goethe-Institut at Campo dos Mártires da Pátria. The photograph shows a dragon tree, Dracaena draco, and it does not look like most trees. The trunk is thick and grey, and it splits into a thicket of forking limbs that run out sideways and then turn up, each ending in a tuft of stiff, sword-shaped leaves. Together they make a dense umbrella that reaches over the garden tables, so the cafe sits in its shade.

queue.note: Inside the Goethe Institute, there’s a beautiful garden rich with bushes, shrubs and trees. The dragon plant is just one of many trees worth seeing there.
